newsitem.title: USA: Forecasts suggest wet weekend for U.S. Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Forecasts suggest wet weekend for U.S. Midwest.

text.p: Forecasts call for a wet weekend in much of the U.S. Midwest, followed by a brief warming period early next week, before being replaced by more rain and cool weather late next week, meterologists said.
"We are not looking for extended warm, dry weather for the Midwest," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Express Inc.
Forecasts called for 0.25 to 1.5 inches of rain from Friday to Sunday over much of the Midwest and Mississippi Delta states, with 60 to 80 percent coverage, meteorologists said.
WSC's Burgio said some computer models suggest a warmup for much of next week with showers and cooler weather late in the period. While other models suggest wet, cool conditions for much of the week.
But, Burgio said he favors forecasts that call for warm weather early next week, with cool, wet conditions later.

Fred Gesser, Weather Express Inc meteorologist, said weather maps suggest normal to above normal temperatures from Illinois to Ohio for much of next week but will be accompanied by above normal precipitation.
Both meteorologists said rain should not interrupt the hard red winter wheat harvest this week in Texas and southern Oklahoma.
"The parts that are harvesting probably won't get rain," said Gesser.
